items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S477

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the court of claims act, the public housing law, the
correction law, and the civil service law, in relation to the availabil-
ity of certain benefits to exonerees; and to repeal certain provisions
of the court of claims act relating thereto

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill will ensure exonerees are entitled to the same re-entry
services as other formerly incarcerated persons, as well as additional
benefits intended to ameliorate their wrongful conviction

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the Court of Claims Act to add a new section that
defines "exoneree."

Section 2 updates the language in subdivision 5 of section 8-b of the
Court of Claims Act to ensure it applies to women.

Section 3 amends subsection 5 of section 8-b to ensure that an exoneree
needs only be cleared of charges they were convicted of to qualify for
benefits.

Section 4 amends section 8-b of the Court of Claims Act to allow for
exonerees who were convicted based on a false confession to qualify for
benefits.

Section 5 repeals subdivision 7 of section 8-b of the Court of Claims
Act.

Section 6 amends section 8-b of the Court of Claims Act to clarify that
the benefits detailed in this legislation will be made available upon
the finding for the claimant by the court.

Section 7 adds ten new subsections 7-16 to the Court of Claims Act,
which will seal the conviction records of exonerees, specify that the
benefits are not taxable and shall not be reduced to compensate for the
costs of their incarceration, establish exoneree eligibility for health
and dental insurance benefits, allow for the repayment of reasonable
attorney's fees incurred in the exoneration process, establish exoneree
eligibility for tuition benefits, establish exoneree eligibility for all
benefits made available to parolees, protect exonerees' right to sue for
damages, allow exonerees to pursue further civil lawsuits, and establish
windows for filing claims and filing for benefits under this section.

Section 8 adds a new paragraph c to subdivision 1 of section 156 of the
Public Housing Law which would prevent any exoneree benefits from being
used to calculate income for public housing eligibility, and ensures
that exonerees will be given the highest need-based priority for place-
ment in public housing units.

Section 9 amends subdivision 4 of section 404 of the correction law
which includes exonerees in the class of inmates that is entitled to
mental health discharge planning and other mental health treatment.
Section 10 amends subdivision 2 of section 163 of the civil service law
to provide for the provision of health insurance to exonerees.

Section 11 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Exonerees, those who have been wrongfully convicted, suffer enormous
damage through no fault of their own. It is the State's responsibility
to do everything possible to correct those wrongs.  While New York's
current policy is better than many other states, it still leaves much of
the burden of re-entry on individual exonerees and their families. This
bill will shift much of this burden back onto the state, rather than on
the exonerees.

Exonerees have a broad variety of needs stemming from their time in
prison. Because prisoners suffer from poor physical and mental health,
it is critical that exonerees are immediately able to access health and
mental health care. Job training and education benefits are also essen-
tial to ensure exonerees are able to get and hold jobs after their
incarceration. Housing is also a serious concern for many exonerees,
since they have often have no income or credit history that would allow
them to rent an apartment on their own.

Some exonerees are able to depend on family or friends as they begin to
rebuild their lives, but many exonerees don't have those resources.
Every person who has been wrongly convicted should have all the support
they need to start fresh.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S.2914 of 2019-2020 (Hoylman): Died in Judiciary)
A.1003 of 2019-2020 (Quart): Died in Judiciary
S.0053-B of 2017-2018 (Hoylman): Died in Judiciary
A.3894-B of 2017-2018 (Quart): Died in Codes
S.7054-A of 2016 (Hoylman): Died in Judiciary
A.9575-A of 2016 (Quart): Died in Ways & Means

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately
